subject: Physics
paperTitle: Paper 3 Section B Option A — Astrophysics
sourceVerification: All 15 part marks and PDF page positions inspected against official AQA June 2022 QP and final mark scheme. Topic codes checked against AQA's current official 3.9 specification; 02.1 is a nearest-section cross-topic mapping, not an exact examiner-issued code.
markingGuidanceOriginalSummary: AQA distinguishes acceptable alternatives from mandatory combined statements, and contradiction can negate an otherwise correct list point.
Calculation credit can include equivalent working and specified follow-through; do not award method marks to a numerical coincidence derived from invalid physics.
Diagram-based and graph-based marks require visible evidence, not just recognised topic words.
Six-mark cosmology response uses overall level descriptors and a calculation condition for top marks.
An answer-only result may be fully credited when allowed by the official scheme, but show-that tasks need the required supporting method.
copyrightNotice: This JSON is an original editorial map of official source parts and does not reproduce AQA question stems, diagrams, answer keys, or marking text. It is not a playable paper.

parts.markingRisk: Diagram must distinguish central and edge-ray focal points; text-only answers cannot establish the geometry.
Three off-axis rays and correctly located shared focal plane are required; do not award all drawing marks from a prose description.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Eyepiece focal length from telescope magnification
parts.markingRisk: Evaluate the coupled magnification and lens-separation equations; a shortcut denominator with no justification is not equivalent.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: CCD and human-eye observations of close binaries
parts.markingRisk: Credit different valid detector trade-offs and their observational consequences; cap answers without a specific consequence.
The relative depth of dips needs an explanation grounded in stellar temperatures, not simply their sizes.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Systematic wavelength shift of an orbiting binary
parts.markingRisk: Direction of the system's overall radial motion matters; a generic Doppler mention alone is not enough.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Radial velocity from a varying spectral line
parts.markingRisk: Use the half-range shift and suitable mean wavelength; accept equivalent valid routes and supported follow-through.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Orbital radius from a periodic light curve
parts.markingRisk: Read the orbital period correctly; accept follow-through from a prior speed and use consistent time units.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Prominent absorption lines in a B-class spectrum
parts.markingRisk: Single-option selection must match stellar spectral classification.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Observational tests for two compact stellar remnants
parts.markingRisk: Require independently relevant properties and a way to link them to the same system.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Radio observation of an early quasar
parts.markingRisk: Specific radio emission property, not generic brightness.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Absolute magnitude from apparent magnitude and distance
parts.markingRisk: Distance units and logarithm argument must be correct; preserve valid algebraic rearrangements.
Use absolute, not apparent, magnitude when comparing equal distances; accept correctly followed rounded values.

parts.editorialSkillLabel: Mean density inside a black-hole event horizon
parts.markingRisk: Track conversion from solar masses to SI mass, event-horizon radius and volume; award appropriate error carried forward.
Six-mark response is level-based and requires coverage of distinct evidence plus a relevant calculation for top bands; do not mark as six independent keywords.
